Question: Isoniazides are degraded by CYP2E1. What happens to the half-life of isoniazides in individuals with reduced catalytic capacity of CYP2E1?

Options:
A. because isoniazides are less degraded, the half-life decreases
B. the half-life increases
C. the half-life remains unchanged, but the volume of distribution decreases
D. the half-life remains unchanged, but the volume of distribution increases

Thought: I need to understand what happens to the half-life of a drug when the enzyme that degrades it has reduced catalytic capacity.

The half-life of a drug is the time it takes for its concentration in the body to be reduced by half. When an enzyme that metabolizes (degrades) a drug has reduced catalytic capacity, the drug will be metabolized more slowly.

In this case, isoniazides are degraded by CYP2E1. If individuals have reduced catalytic capacity of CYP2E1, then:
- The enzyme will degrade isoniazides more slowly
- The drug will stay in the body longer
- The elimination rate will decrease
- The half-life will increase (since half-life = ln(2)/elimination rate)

When the elimination rate decreases, the half-life increases. This is because it takes longer for the body to clear half of the drug.

Looking at the options:
A. Suggests half-life decreases - incorrect, as slower degradation means longer half-life
B. Suggests half-life increases - correct, as explained above
C and D. Suggest half-life remains unchanged - incorrect, as half-life definitely changes when elimination rate changes
Final Answer: [ANSWER]B[/ANSWER]
